nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be coprime integers, let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{2n} (-1)^j x^{4n-2j} y^{2j}$, that is, $S = x^{4n} - x^{4n-2} y^2 + \cdots - x^2 y^{4n-2} + y^{4n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are coprime natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.
nodes.title: An alternating sum in coprime integers $x, y$ is a sum of two coprime squares

nodes.summary: Alternating geometric sums for primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and odd $n$ are differences of two squares. Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and let $n$ be a positive odd integer. Then there are integers $a, b$ with $\sum_{j=0}^{p-1} (-1)^j p^{nj} = 1 - p^n + p^{2n} - \cdots + p^{(p-1)n} = a^2 - b^2$.
nodes.title: Alternating geometric sums for primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and odd $n$ are differences of two squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $n$ be a positive odd integer, let $k$ be a positive integer, and put $q = p^k$. Then there are integers $a, b$ with $\sum_{j=0}^{q-1} (-1)^j p^{nj} = 1 - p^n + p^{2n} - \cdots + p^{(q-1)n} = a^2 + b^2$.
nodes.title: Alternating geometric sums with $p^k$ terms, $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, as sums of two squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $n \ge 0$ be an integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{p-1} (-1)^j p^{nj} = 1 - p^n + p^{2n} - \cdots + p^{(p-1)n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.
nodes.title: Alternating geometric sums for primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ are sums of two squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $n$ be a positive even integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{p-1} (-1)^j p^{nj} = 1 - p^n + p^{2n} - \cdots + p^{(p-1)n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are coprime natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.
nodes.title: Alternating geometric sums for odd primes $p$ and even $n$ are sums of two coprime squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $X_1 = \sum_{i=0}^{(p-1)/2} (-1)^i x^{p-1-2i}$ and $Y_1 = \sum_{i=0}^{(p-3)/2} (-1)^i x^{p-2-2i}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, and let $\Phi_{4p}$ be the $4p$-th cyclotomic polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$. Then $\Phi_{4p} = X_1^2 + Y_1^2$.
nodes.title: The cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_{4p}$ as a sum of two explicit squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k \ge 1$, let $X_1 = \sum_{i=0}^{(p-1)/2} (-1)^i x^{p-1-2i}$ and $Y_1 = \sum_{i=0}^{(p-3)/2} (-1)^i x^{p-2-2i}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, and let $\Phi_{4p^k}$ be the $4p^k$-th cyclotomic polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$. Then $\Phi_{4p^k}(x) = X_1\bigl(x^{p^{k-1}}\bigr)^2 + Y_1\bigl(x^{p^{k-1}}\bigr)^2$.
nodes.title: The cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_{4p^k}$ as a sum of two explicit squares

nodes.summary: For every integer $q \ge 1$ there are polynomials $A, B \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that the $4q$-th cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_{4q}$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ satisfies $\Phi_{4q} = A^2 + B^2$.
nodes.title: Every cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_{4q}$ is a sum of two squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, let $n$ be a positive odd integer, let $k$ be a positive integer, and put $q = p^k$. Then there are integers $a, b$ with $\sum_{j=0}^{q-1} p^{nj} = 1 + p^n + p^{2n} + \cdots + p^{(q-1)n} = a^2 + b^2$.
nodes.title: Geometric sums with $p^k$ terms, $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and $n$ odd, are sums of two squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, let $n$ be a positive odd integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{p-1} p^{nj} = 1 + p^n + p^{2n} + \cdots + p^{(p-1)n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.
nodes.title: Geometric sums for primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and odd $n$ are sums of two squares
